name: basil cottage cheese spread
instructions:
A settled spreadable cheese base — an easy win. 2:1 COTTAGE CHEESE TO CREAM CHEESE + basil (leaves AND stems) + black pepper + garlic powder, food-processed. NO SALT (see notes). Built for the heirloom tomato tartine ([[tartine]] variant E) but excellent as a general spread.

=== INGREDIENTS (SETTLED RATIOS) ===

- 2 parts cottage cheese
- 1 part cream cheese
- fresh basil — LEAVES + STEMS both (the stems process in fine)
- freshly cracked black pepper
- garlic powder (NOT fresh garlic — see notes)
- NO SALT (the cheeses carry enough — see notes)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. FOOD PROCESS: cottage cheese + cream cheese + basil (leaves and stems) + black pepper + garlic powder until integrated and spreadable. The cottage curds smooth out; the basil flecks through.
2. SPREAD: on toasted bread. Top with sliced ripe tomato (heirloom when in season) for the tartine use case — see [[tartine]] variant E.
notes:
=== SETTLED — AN EASY WIN (THE OLYMPICS CONCLUDED FAST) ===

This recipe started as a stub with a mission ('the spreadable cheese olympics' — find the perfect spreadable base for an heirloom tomato tartine). It resolved on essentially the first serious attempt: 2:1 cottage-to-cream-cheese + basil leaves-and-stems + black pepper + garlic powder, no salt. A really amazing spread overall. No need to keep experimenting with more cheese types — the two-cheese answer is the answer.

=== THE SETTLED CALLS ===

- 2:1 COTTAGE TO CREAM CHEESE: cottage-heavy, not cream-cheese-heavy. The cottage cheese brings the lighter body and protein; the cream cheese binds and thickens. This ratio lands spreadable-but-fresh rather than dense.
- BASIL LEAVES + STEMS: both go in. The stems process down fine in the food processor and carry plenty of basil flavor — no reason to pick leaves off stems for this.
- GARLIC POWDER, NOT FRESH GARLIC: this spread is UNCOOKED, and raw fresh garlic would be overpowering — there's no cook step to mellow it. Garlic powder gives the allium presence at a civilized intensity. (Same raw-garlic caution as other no-cook preparations.)
- NO SALT: the cheeses carry enough salt on their own. Adding salt on autopilot over-salts it — same lesson as [[mexicanized-romesco]]'s canned-pepper salting failure mode: taste before you salt anything built on pre-salted ingredients.
- BLACK PEPPER: yes — the one seasoning besides garlic powder it wants.

=== LEMON JUICE — WOULD GO WELL, DOESN'T NEED IT ===

Lemon juice would pair well with the spread (bright acid against the creamy-herby base) but the spread doesn't NEED it — it's complete as-is. Add a small squeeze if you want the brighter version; skip freely. Kept in want-to-try as an optional direction rather than part of the recipe.

=== COMPARISON — [[tomato-tart]]'S CHEESE STACK IS OPTIMIZED FOR BAKING, THIS IS OPTIMIZED FOR SPREADING ===

The [[tomato-tart]] uses a three-cheese base (parmesan + ricotta + mozzarella) under shingled tomatoes — same cheese-under-tomato idea, but optimized to be BAKEABLE: ricotta holds structure in the oven, mozzarella melts, parmesan sharpens. It's a cooked format.

THIS spread is the RAW / SPREADABLE counterpart: no bake, so the optimization flips — cream cheese (which would be wrong in a baked tart) is exactly right here as the binder, and cottage cheese leads. The two recipes are the two poles of cheese-under-tomato:
- BAKEABLE (tomato-tart): ricotta-led, oven-structured
- SPREADABLE (this): cottage-led + cream-cheese-bound, knife-structured

=== RELATED FORMATS ===

- [[tartine]]: variant E (heirloom tomato tartine) is this spread's home use case — thick layer on toast, ripe tomato on top.
- [[sardine-cream-cheese-spread]]: the other cream-cheese-based spread in the cookbook — savory-fishy direction.
- Bruschetta (no recipe yet): the italian reference point — classically no cheese at all (garlic-rubbed toast + tomato + basil + oil). This spread version is deliberately richer.
why_i_like_this_recipe: An easy win — settled on the first serious attempt. Five ingredients, no cook step, and it makes the heirloom tomato tartine work.
